Tithing (Doctrine)
TAI-thing
noun (Christian ethics)
The biblical practice of giving a tenth (tithe) of one's increase to the LORD. Established in the patriarchal period (Abraham's tithe to Melchizedek, Genesis 14:20; Jacob's vow, Genesis 28:22), codified in the Mosaic law (Leviticus 27:30-33; Numbers 18; Deuteronomy 14), and discussed in the NT. The contemporary debate concerns whether the tithe remains binding under the New Covenant or whether NT giving is governed by proportional cheerful generosity.

📖 Biblical Definition

The biblical practice of giving a tenth (tithe) of one's increase to the LORD. The tithe predates the Mosaic law (Abraham's tithe to Melchizedek, Genesis 14:20, cited in Hebrews 7; Jacob's vow to tithe, Genesis 28:22), was codified in the Mosaic law (Leviticus 27:30-33, the tithe of the land belongs to the LORD; Numbers 18:21-24, the tithe given to the Levites; Deuteronomy 14:22-29, the festival tithe and the third-year poor-tithe), and is discussed in the NT (Matthew 23:23, the Lord Jesus affirms the tithe while rebuking the Pharisees for tithing herbs while neglecting justice, mercy, and faith; Hebrews 7, Abraham's tithe to Melchizedek as a type of Christ's superior priesthood). The contemporary Christian debate concerns whether the tithe remains binding under the New Covenant. (1) The continuing-tithe position: the tithe is a creation-and-patriarchal ordinance predating the Mosaic law, affirmed by Christ (Matthew 23:23), and continuing as the baseline of Christian giving; the New Covenant believer gives at least a tithe. (2) The proportional-generosity position: the specific tithe was part of the Mosaic ceremonial-civil law that has expired; NT giving is governed by proportional cheerful generosity (2 Corinthians 9:7; 1 Corinthians 16:2, as God hath prospered him), which may be more or less than a tithe depending on the believer's means. The patriarchal-Reformed reader engages the debate with substantive seriousness, recognizing the substantive arguments on both sides. The substantive consensus: Christian giving should be regular, proportional, sacrificial, cheerful, and substantial; the tithe (a tenth) is a substantive and historic baseline for Christian giving; the believer of substantial means should give substantially more than a tithe; the principal substantive concern is the substantive grace of generous giving to the church, the poor, and the missionary cause (2 Corinthians 8-9), not legalistic tithe-calculation.

TITHING (DOCTRINE), n. (Christian ethics) Giving a tenth (tithe) of one's increase to the LORD. Predates the Mosaic law (Abraham's tithe to Melchizedek, Genesis 14:20, cited Hebrews 7; Jacob's vow, Genesis 28:22); codified in Mosaic law (Leviticus 27:30-33; Numbers 18; Deuteronomy 14); affirmed by Christ (Matthew 23:23, while rebuking Pharisees for tithing herbs while neglecting justice, mercy, faith). Contemporary debate: (1) continuing-tithe position (a creation-patriarchal ordinance predating Moses, affirmed by Christ, continuing as the baseline); (2) proportional-generosity position (the specific tithe was Mosaic ceremonial-civil law now expired; NT giving governed by proportional cheerful generosity, 2 Corinthians 9:7; 1 Corinthians 16:2). Consensus: giving regular, proportional, sacrificial, cheerful, substantial.

📖 Key Scripture

Malachi 3:8-10 — "Will a man rob God? Yet ye have robbed me. But ye say, Wherein have we robbed thee? In tithes and offerings... Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in mine house, and prove me now herewith, saith the LORD of hosts, if I will not open you the windows of heaven."

Matthew 23:23 — "Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone."

2 Corinthians 9:7 — "Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver."

Genesis 14:20 — "And blessed be the most high God, which hath delivered thine enemies into thy hand. And he gave him tithes of all."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The tithing debate is substantive within the Christian tradition; the contemporary church suffers from substantive under-giving regardless of position; the consensus is regular, proportional, sacrificial, cheerful, substantial giving with the tithe as a historic baseline.

expand to see more

The tithing debate is a substantive intra-Christian discussion with substantive arguments on both sides. The continuing-tithe position holds that the tithe is a creation-and-patriarchal ordinance predating the Mosaic law (Abraham and Jacob both tithed before the law), affirmed by Christ (Matthew 23:23), and continuing as the baseline of Christian giving. The proportional-generosity position holds that the specific tithe was part of the Mosaic ceremonial-civil law (which funded the Levitical priesthood and the festival-and-poor system) that has expired with the change of the priesthood, and that NT giving is governed by proportional cheerful generosity (2 Corinthians 9:7; 1 Corinthians 16:2). The patriarchal-Reformed reader recognizes the substantive arguments on both sides and holds the substantive consensus: Christian giving should be regular, proportional, sacrificial, cheerful, and substantial; the tithe (a tenth) is a substantive and historic baseline; the believer of substantial means should give substantially more than a tithe. The principal substantive concern is not the legalistic calculation of the tithe but the substantive grace of generous giving (2 Corinthians 8-9) to the church, the poor, and the missionary cause. The contemporary church suffers from substantive under-giving (the average professing Christian gives a fraction of a tithe); the substantive recovery is the recovery of generous, sacrificial, regular, substantial giving as a substantive grace of the Christian life.
